newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money stable at 3.10 pct in slim trade.
newsitem.headline: German call money stable at 3.10 pct in slim trade.

text.p: German call money rates remained stable at around 3.10 percent on Monday as government demand continued to underpin a quiet market, dealers said.
"It is pretty quiet here," said one trader. "We're staying with around 3.08 to 3.12 percent, although some small trades have gone through under 3.10 percent."
Although a certain amount of government demand was reported ahead of the transfer of Bundesbank profits -- due on Thursday -- sufficient deposits ensured rates were kept stable.
Traders said this situation was likely to continue for the next few sessions.
"The liquidity looks reasonably good, so there is no reason for any tightening in the market," said another dealer.

On Friday, banks held 40.1 billion marks at the Bundesbank, up from a total of 39.1 billion marks on Thursday. The average holdings for the month stood at 41.1 billion marks, easing from Thursday's 41.4 billion level.
Borrowing on the bank's Lombard facility was negligible.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average (FIONA) was calculated at 3.13567 percent on Monday, down slightly from Friday's 3.14300 percent.
